title: Trovata Pricing in 2026: What It Actually Costs
summary: Trovata has a reported base price near $24k/year, but cost scales with bank connections, accounts, and TMS modules. The base package, add-ons, and total cost, broken down.
body_markdown:
Trovata is a modern, API-native cash management platform, and it is unusual in its category for having a published base price rather than a pure "talk to sales" model. But the base is only the entry point, and the real cost of **Trovata pricing** scales with your bank connections, accounts, transaction volume, and modules. This guide breaks down what Trovata actually costs, from the base package to the add-ons.


A note on sourcing: the figures below come from third-party trackers reporting Trovata's published base tier and estimating the add-ons. Treat the add-on ranges as directional, and confirm your scope in a quote.


## **How much does Trovata cost?**


> Third-party trackers report a Trovata base package around $24,000 per year, covering one bank connection, 100 accounts, roughly a million stored transactions, and 10 users, with balances, transaction analysis, reconciliation, and cash positioning. Beyond that, cost scales through quote-based add-ons for more banks, accounts, seats, and enterprise TMS modules, so a multi-bank treasury team can land well into six figures.


> **If the add-ons stack up beyond what your process needs, Concourse is the AI-agent alternative.** Instead of a per-bank, per-module treasury subscription, Concourse connects to your existing ERP, data warehouse, and banking data and runs cash forecasting, variance analysis, and reporting end to end, with scoped pricing.


## **How Trovata pricing works**


Trovata uses a tiered subscription: a published base package, then quote-based add-ons. The cost is driven by:


- **Bank connections.** The base covers one bank; additional bank connectivity is a primary cost driver.
- **Accounts and transactions.** The base caps at 100 accounts and about a million stored transactions; more raises the price.
- **User seats.** The base includes 10 users; additional seats cost extra.
- **TMS modules.** Enterprise modules (debt, investments, FX, deeper TMS coverage) are significant add-ons.


## **Trovata cost estimates**


Based on third-party trackers like[SoftwareFinder](https://softwarefinder.com/enterprise-resource-planning-software/trovata) :


Component Estimated cost Notes


Base package ~$24,000 / year 1 bank, 100 accounts, ~1M transactions, 10 users


Connectivity / usage add-ons ~$5,000 to $15,000 / year Extra banks, accounts, seats


Enterprise TMS modules ~$20,000 to $75,000 / year Debt, investments, FX, full TMS


ERP / custom integration ~$2,000 to $10,000 One-time


The base figure is the most consistently cited number, but it is reported by third-party trackers rather than confirmed on Trovata's own site, so verify it in a quote. The add-on ranges are estimates. The key point: the $24,000 base caps at one bank and ten users, which most multi-bank treasury teams outgrow quickly.


## **Is Trovata worth the price?**


For a midsize-to-large company that wants modern, API-native multi-bank cash visibility without a heavy legacy TMS, Trovata often is worth it. The published base makes budgeting easier than most treasury software, and the platform is quick to deploy relative to enterprise incumbents.


The trade-off is how fast the add-ons stack once you connect multiple banks and turn on the full TMS. If you are looking at Trovata pricing and the modules are adding up, the real question is whether you need a full TMS or just the forecasting and reporting on top of your cash data. ## **Frequently asked questions**


### **How much does Trovata cost?**


Third-party trackers report a base package around $24,000 per year (one bank, 100 accounts, about a million transactions, 10 users). Beyond that, cost scales with additional banks, accounts, seats, and enterprise TMS modules, so an enterprise deployment can reach six figures.


### **Does Trovata publish its pricing?**


Partially. Unusually for treasury software, a base-tier price (around $24,000 per year) is reported for Trovata, but everything beyond the base, extra banks, accounts, seats, and full TMS modules, is quote-based. Confirm the base and add-ons in a quote.


### **Why does Trovata get more expensive?**


Because the base package caps at one bank, 100 accounts, and 10 users. Multi-bank treasury teams quickly add connectivity, accounts, seats, and TMS modules, each of which is a quote-based add-on, so the real cost can land well above the base.


### **Is there a cheaper alternative to Trovata?**


It depends on your need. AI-agent platforms like Concourse run treasury analytics, forecasting, and reporting across your existing systems with scoped pricing rather than a per-bank, per-module subscription. See[Trovata alternatives](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/trovata-alternatives) for the full field.


## **The bottom line**


Trovata pricing is more transparent than most treasury software, with a reported base around $24,000 a year, but that base caps at one bank and ten users. The real cost scales through add-ons for connectivity, accounts, seats, and TMS modules, which can push an enterprise deployment into six figures. For modern multi-bank visibility it can be a strong fit; just model the add-ons, not the base.
